title: Internal modules inherit functorial flat resolutions
statement: Let C be a locally v-small Grothendieck abelian category with an additive closed symmetric monoidal structure, and R a commutative monoid object of C. Let Mod(C,R) be the category of left internal R-modules, with its relative tensor product defined as the coequalizer of the two R-actions. Suppose C admits a functor to its full subcategory of flat objects together with a natural epimorphism from that functor to the identity. Here flat means that both tensor functors are exact. Then Mod(C,R) admits such a functor and natural epimorphism as well.

proof.text: For a module M and ambient object F, exhibit the underlying action map M.X tensor (R tensor F) to M.X tensor F as a split coequalizer of the action and multiplication maps. The splitting inserts the unit to the right of M and to the right of R. Associativity of the right module action gives the relation; the two unit axioms give the section identities. This works also for zero objects and the zero algebra.

The underlying relative tensor coequalizer and the preceding split coequalizer yield an isomorphism (M tensor_R free(F)).X isomorphic to M.X tensor F. Its composite with the quotient is the action map, so epimorphic cancellation proves naturality in M. If F is flat, the right-hand functor preserves finite limits, and forget R reflects them. The braiding handles tensoring on the other side. Closedness supplies preservation of finite colimits on both sides, hence free(F) is flat.

Choose the given functorial flat resolution Lambda in C, whose resolution object is determined up to natural isomorphism by its specification only insofar as this is the supplied structure; no object is chosen from an unproved theorem. Define the actual module-resolution functor as forget R, then Lambda.F, then the inclusion of flat objects, then free R. Lift this explicit composite to the full subcategory of flat modules by the preceding flatness proof.

Define its natural transformation at M as free applied to Lambda.pi at M.X followed by the free-forget counit at M. Functoriality, naturality of Lambda.pi, and counit naturality prove naturality. Free preserves epimorphisms because it is a left adjoint; the counit is epi by its split underlying map and the existing epi counit instance. Their composite is epi. Bundle the functor, transformation and epi proofs into HasFunctorialFlatResolution.
